processing: A green tea; the exact method is not well recorded in accessible references. As with other Chinese greens, the leaf is fixed by heat, rolled and dried.
harvest_season: As is usual for Hubei greens, spring picking is the most valued; exact dates are not recorded.
appearance_dry: Little is recorded; typical of Hubei spring greens, expect slim, dark green leaf.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Hubei green tea, a clear pale yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Typical of spring green tea: tender, fresh green buds and leaves.
taste_profile: Few independent tasting notes exist. Expect what is typical of mountain spring greens from the Dabie range: fresh, gently vegetal and lightly sweet.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for spring green tea. Keep the water below boiling and the early steeps short.

vintage_note: As with other Chinese greens, it is sold as the current year's spring harvest, with the earliest pickings usually costing more. Drink it within the year. Check for Yingshan origin and a clear picking date, because yunwu is a generic term used across China.
description:
Yingshan Yunwu is the signature green tea of Yingshan county in the Dabie Mountains of eastern Hubei. The county is full of tea gardens, and the tea is recognised as its local speciality. Yunwu means cloud and mist.

That word is used for many Chinese teas, including the unrelated Lu Shan Yun Wu, so the place name is what matters here. Don't assume two yunwu teas have anything else in common.

The method is not spelled out in accessible references, so treat it as typical green tea work: fix, roll, dry. A cup should taste like a mountain spring green, fresh and gently sweet. Too much heat makes this kind of tea flat and bitter.

Buy the current spring, and ask for the producer and the picking date. A county-level brand covers a wide range of quality. If you are curious about the plants behind it, Yingshan's old seed-grown population is a good thing to ask about.
history: Little is documented in accessible records about the tea's early history. What is firm is its modern status: in 2022 China's National Intellectual Property Administration approved a national demonstration zone for protecting Yingshan Yunwu as a geographical indication product.
